headline: AZTEC DRILLS 155m AT 1.63 g/t AuEq — Tombstone Oxide Zone Expands West, South, SW; Shallow Heap-Leach Grade System Growing Fast (CVE:AZT)
snippet: Aztec Minerals Corp. (CVE: AZT) released results from 11 drill holes at the Contention zone of its Tombstone Property in southeastern Arizona, with the best hole returning 155.4 metres averaging 1.08 g/t Au and 30.23 g/t Ag (1.63 g/t AuEq) within a broader 198.1-metre zone at 0.86 g/t Au — near-surface oxide mineralization that is prospective for low-cost heap-leach processing. Step-out and first-pass holes extended the system to the west, southwest, and south of previously reported holes, while core hole TC25-03 also confirmed CRD sulfide targets at depth. Kappes, Cassiday & Associates has been engaged for metallurgical testwork as the company moves toward a resource estimate.

headline: PORTUGAL TUNGSTEN: FIRST 2026 HOLE HITS 23.8m AT 0.68% WO₃ — Allied Critical Opens Borralha With High-Grade Core of 2.96% WO₃; 6 Rigs Running (CSE:ACM)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Allied Critical Metals
snippet: Allied Critical Metals Inc. (CSE: ACM) released the first assay results from its 2026 drilling campaign at the Santa Helena Breccia within its Borralha Tungsten Project in northern Portugal, with drill hole Bo_13/26 returning 23.8 metres grading 0.68% WO₃ from 24.0 metres — including a 4.0-metre core at 2.96% WO₃ — within a broad 57.6-metre corridor at 0.30% WO₃. Six rigs are operating with a seventh arriving shortly, targeting resource conversion, geotechnical work, and metallurgical sampling simultaneously; parallel exploration continues at the newly discovered Venise Breccia 400 metres to the northwest. Tungsten is an EU critical raw material with 80% of global refining controlled by China, and Borralha is one of the few advanced tungsten projects in a Western jurisdiction.

headline: NALUNAQ CONFIRMS 132.5 g/t Au UNDERGROUND — 30% of Stope Holes Above 60 g/t Au; 42.8 g/t Block Average Locks In Near-Term Mining Plan (LSE:AMRQ)
snippet: Amaroq Minerals Ltd. (LSE/CSE: AMRQ) released underground drill results from its Nalunaq gold mine in Greenland, with 37 holes on the 802 and 773 Levels confirming exceptional high-grade continuity: 16 of 37 holes exceeded 30 g/t Au (the average MRE4 resource grade), 30% exceeded 60 g/t Au, and best intercepts included 132.5 g/t Au over 0.50 metres and 132.0 g/t Au over 0.50 metres. The Mountain Block delivered a 42.8 g/t Au average, directly underpinning 27 planned stopes on Level 802 and 10 on Level 773. Underground drilling will next relocate to the 810 Level, where the western stopes of the near-term mine plan require geological confidence drilling.

headline: CHILE COPPER COLLAPSES 12.9% IN MAY — Output Hits 3-Year Low as Grade Declines, Water Shortages Bite; Futures Tag $6.34/lb Three-Week High
snippet: Copper futures hit $6.34 per pound on July 16 — three-week highs — as Chile's national copper production fell 12.9% year-over-year in May to 423,623 metric tonnes, extending a broad-based sequential decline (down 9% in March, 13.8% in April) that is cutting across both state-owned and private operations simultaneously. Cochilco attributed the drop to a combination of water shortages, falling ore grades, transitions from oxide to sulphide mining, unplanned maintenance, and labour disputes. Chile accounts for roughly 50% of global copper exports; with no rapid production recovery expected, tightening near-term supply is the dominant price driver heading into H2 2026.

headline: VIOR EXTENDS LIGNERIS SOUTH ZONE TO 1,300m LATERAL — Quebec Abitibi Hole Returns 7.37 g/t Au Over 2.0m at 564m Depth; 6,000 Assays Pending (CVE:VIO)
snippet: Vior Gold Corporation (CVE: VIO) announced that two new holes from its 30,000-metre program at the 100%-owned Ligneris Project, 55 km northwest of Amos in Quebec's Abitibi region, have extended the South Zone to more than 1,300 metres of lateral strike: hole LI-26-034 intersected 7.37 g/t Au over 2.0 metres (including 12.6 g/t Au over 1.0 metre) at 564 metres depth, while LI-26-024 returned 5.17 g/t Au over 2.9 metres and extended mineralization 100 metres further west. With 23,600 metres completed and more than 6,000 assays pending at the laboratory, the program is on track to finish in Q3 2026.

headline: FOUNDERS METALS CONFIRMS ANTINO NORTHEAST — Discovery Hole Hits 58.5m AT 1.00 g/t Au; New Zone Opens 4th Front on Suriname Gold System (TSXV:FDR)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Founders Metals Inc.
snippet: Founders Metals Inc. (TSXV: FDR) released a mid-year exploration update from its 70,000-metre 2026 drill program at the Antino Gold Project in southeastern Suriname, confirming a new discovery at Antino Northeast where hole ANE009 returned 58.5 metres at 1.00 g/t Au from 18.6 metres depth, with a second hole 1,200 metres away hitting 53.0 metres at 0.46 g/t Au — establishing a third new discovery zone in 2026 alongside Antino West (53.1m at 1.21 g/t Au from surface) and the earlier Antino North finds. With four targets now active across the project and ounces accumulating across a large footprint, Founders continues to build the resource geometry for what is emerging as a district-scale gold system.

headline: REDCASTLE DELIVERS COSTERFIELD-STYLE GOLD 250m DEEP — First Drill Below Water Table Confirms Multi-Vein System to 321m; Victoria Belt Grows (TSX:SXGC)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Southern Cross Gold Consolidated
snippet: Southern Cross Gold Consolidated (TSX: SXGC / ASX: SX2) announced results from two drill holes beneath the historic Redcastle Goldfield in Victoria, Australia — the first holes drilled below the water table at the Laura prospect — confirming Costerfield-style gold-antimony-bearing veins over more than 250 metres of vertical extent. Best intercepts include 26.2 g/t Au over 0.14 metres at 112.98 metres and 15.4 g/t Au over 0.22 metres at 321.84 metres. Redcastle lies 64 km north-northwest of the company's flagship Sunday Creek project and significantly expands the footprint of high-grade structurally-controlled gold mineralisation along Victoria's prolific gold belt.

headline: ISS GREENLIGHTS EQUINOX-ORLA MERGER — July 22 Vote Set; $18.5B Gold Giant With 1M+ oz/Year One Week From Creation (TSX:EQX, NYSE:ORLA)
snippet: Independent proxy advisory firms including ISS have recommended Equinox Gold (TSX: EQX) shareholders vote FOR the share issuance resolution to acquire Orla Mining (NYSE/TSX: ORLA) in a share-for-share deal, ahead of a special meeting scheduled for July 22, 2026 in Vancouver. Under the arrangement, each Orla share converts to 1.00 Equinox share, leaving Orla holders with approximately 33% of the combined company. If approved, the merger creates a senior North American gold producer with a combined market value of US$18.5 billion, projected annual output exceeding one million ounces from six operating mines in Canada, the USA, Nicaragua, and Mexico, with the deal expected to close in Q3 2026 subject to remaining regulatory conditions.

headline: AMERICAN URANIUM ADVANCES LO HERMA ISR — Unit 1 Pump Testing Clears Key Milestone at Wyoming In-Situ Recovery Project
snippet: American Uranium Inc. announced the successful completion of Mine Unit 1 pump testing at its Lo Herma In-Situ Recovery (ISR) uranium project in Wyoming, advancing the project toward initial production. The milestone clears a critical development hurdle for one of the lowest-capital-intensity uranium production methods — ISR involves dissolving uranium in place and pumping it to surface, eliminating conventional open-pit or underground mining costs. The advancement arrives as U.S. uranium demand from nuclear utilities continues to rise and domestic supply remains limited, with term contract pricing remaining firm despite softness in spot prices.

headline: ALL 18 RARE EARTH PRICES SURGE IN JULY — Germanium +27.8%, Dysprosium +25.4%, 16.7% Average Gain; First Broad-Based Rally of 2026 as China Quota Looms
snippet: Every one of the 18 rare earth elements tracked rose in price in July 2026 — the first genuinely broad-based advance of the year — led by germanium (+27.8%), indium (+26.5%), and dysprosium (+25.4%), with an average basket gain of 16.7% and a median of 18.1%. The rally reflects continued Chinese export controls, a stark ex-China price bifurcation (heavy rare earths outside China trade at up to five times the domestic price), and pre-positioning ahead of China's MIIT H2 mining quota announcement, which had not been released as of the July update. A quota reduction would extend the price surge; an expansion would cap it — making the upcoming announcement the sector's most important near-term catalyst.

headline: STEER: SILVER DEFICIT HITS YEAR 6 — Gold, Silver Ready to Bottom in July/August; Triple-Digit Silver Still Possible by Year-End If Commercials Stand Aside
snippet: Veteran precious metals analyst Ed Steer, writing for Money Metals Exchange and republished at GoldSeek, argues that gold and silver are approaching a cyclical bottom that should resolve higher by late summer — with silver in its sixth consecutive year of structural supply deficit where global consumption consistently exceeds mine production. Steer highlights tightening physical markets, the gradual shift of pricing authority from Western futures exchanges to Asian physical buyers, and unsustainable government debt trajectories as the structural case, while noting that commercial traders on the COMEX holding large short positions are the primary near-term obstacle to a sustained rally. He expects silver could return to triple-digit prices before year-end if those short positions are allowed to cover without triggering a reversal.
